This can be from a number of different reasons. One of the usual suspects is that you have some sort of program that integrates with Explorer (using what's called Hooks) that has a bug which causes Explorer to crash. Example of a hook is WinRar which adds menu items to the context menu in explorer (like "Add to RAR")

Drive defragmentation is still scheduled by default even though I only have a SSD. Even my old Tuneup Utilities from 2013 recognized my SSD and automatically disabled scheduled defragmentation.

You need to read up on what Windows does to SSD drives. It doesn't defragment them, but it does something else ("Optimise") which you need to keep enabled or the performance of your drives will degrade, because that's how SSD's work.

SSD disks perform worse the more data is stored on it. In file systems, files doesn't get physically deleted when you delete a file, it just marks allocation units as "free". The SSD however isn't aware of filesystems, so the operating system needs to notify the SSD drives which areas can safely be physically deleted. It's expensive to do this every time a file is deleted, so Windows just keeps a record of which allocations can be freed by the SSD and then calls a function in the SSD drive firmware called TRIM. Mac OS and Linux does the exact same thing.
